root_cause_label: Heuristic-Based Strategy Failed Tight Performance Thresholds
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent adopted a greedy most-common-shape selection plus ratio-based gen_len merging strategy at step 17, never incorporating cost-model-aligned dynamic programming, and submitted a solution at step 59 that still violated multiple thresholds while incorrectly claiming near-threshold performance was sufficient.
t_err_evidence: cat > optimized_packer.py: heuristic shape selection by most-common aligned prompt sizes and gen_len grouping
t_commit_evidence: All subsequent versions (v2 through final2, steps 22-50) preserve the same most-common-frequency shape selection core and only adjust the gen_len ratio threshold parameter; the failing algorithmic skeleton is locked in at step 17 and is never reconsidered.
t_surface_evidence: Sequential Timecost 2.9717e+08 (target 2.7e8); Bucket 2 Pad Ratio 0.1693 (target 0.15) over thresholds
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked the domain insight that minimizing the cost model's decode cost plus per-batch overhead requires cost-model-aware shape selection (e.g., k-medoids/weighted-quantile always including global S_max=2048) combined with DP batch segmentation, not a simple frequency-count heuristic. The counting heuristic cannot systematically minimize sequential_timecost.
